title: HW 22
subtitle: Ch. 9 — Enthalpy, Heats of Formation & Hess's Law

questions.q: Match the terms.
items: describes heat energy transfer for a specific number of moles in a system
typically has a unit of joules
describes the sum of all heat transferred into and out of a system
typically has a unit of kJ or kJ/mol
questions.note: Enthalpy (ΔH) = heat per reaction as written (specific moles), in kJ or kJ/mol. Heat energy (q) = total heat in/out, usually in J.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct statement for a chemical reaction that absorbs heat?
opts: The reaction is exothermic with a positive ΔH.
The reaction is endothermic with a negative ΔH.
The reaction is endothermic with ΔH = 0.
The reaction is endothermic with a positive ΔH.
The reaction is exothermic with a negative ΔH.
questions.note: Absorbs heat = endothermic = +ΔH.

questions.q: Where would you write the word 'heat' in these equations?
items: C₃H₈ (g) + 5 O₂ (g) → 3 CO₂ (g) + 4 H₂O (l)   ΔH = 2219.2 kJ
4 HCl (g) + O₂ (g) → 2 H₂O + 2 Cl₂ (g)   ΔH = −202.5 kJ
opts: to the RIGHT of the arrow
to the LEFT of the arrow
questions.note: Negative ΔH (exothermic) → heat is a product (right side). Positive ΔH (endothermic) → heat is a reactant (left side).

questions.q: Label each reaction exothermic or endothermic.
items: C₃H₈ (g) + 5 O₂ (g) → 3 CO₂ (g) + 4 H₂O (l)   ΔH = 2219.2 kJ
4 HCl (g) + O₂ (g) → 2 H₂O + 2 Cl₂ (g)   ΔH = −202.5 kJ
questions.note: Negative ΔH = exothermic; positive ΔH = endothermic.

questions.q: The energy has been written into each equation. Which are correctly written?
items: 2 CO₂ (g) − 566.0 kJ → 2 CO (g) + O₂ (g)   ΔH = 566.0 kJ
4 HCl (g) + O₂ (g) → 2 H₂O + 2 Cl₂ (g) − 202.5 kJ   ΔH = −202.5 kJ
H₂ (g) + Cl₂ (g) → 2 HCl (g) + 184.6 kJ   ΔH = −184.6 kJ
C₃H₈ (g) + 5 O₂ (g) + 2219.2 kJ → 3 CO₂ (g) + 4 H₂O (l)   ΔH = 2219.2 kJ
questions.note: Energy written inside an equation is always ADDED (+) on the correct side, never subtracted. Endothermic → + kJ on the left; exothermic → + kJ on the right.

questions.q: Flashback: standard conditions for thermodynamics.

blanks.label: Standard temperature for thermodynamics in °C (number only)
Standard pressure for thermodynamics in atm (number only)
Is the enthalpy standard temperature the same as gas STP temperature? (yes/no)

questions.note: Thermodynamic standard state = 25 °C and 1 atm. Gas STP = 0 °C and 1 atm, so the temperatures are different.

questions.q: If 163.2 g of a new chemical 'ACO₂' is produced by AC + O₂ → ACO₂ and that reaction releases 517.2 kJ of energy, what is the enthalpy change (kJ)?
questions.note: 163.2 g ÷ 184.2 g/mol = 0.8860 mol ACO₂. ΔH = −517.2 kJ ÷ 0.8860 mol = −583.8 kJ (per 1 mol, as written). Negative because heat is released.

questions.q: If 0.9781 g of 'XY₂' is produced by X + 2Y → XY₂ and that reaction absorbs 736.2 J of energy, what is the enthalpy change in kJ (correct sig figs)?
questions.note: 736.2 J = 0.7362 kJ. 0.9781 g ÷ 308.21 g/mol = 0.003173 mol. ΔH = +0.7362 ÷ 0.003173 = 232.0 kJ. Positive because heat is absorbed.
questions.given: XY₂ molar mass = 308.21 g/mol · watch the J → kJ unit!

questions.q: 2 SO₃ (g) → 2 SO₂ (g) + O₂ (g) has an enthalpy change of 198 kJ. How many grams of sulfur dioxide are produced when 564 kJ is absorbed?
questions.note: 564 kJ × (2 mol SO₂ / 198 kJ) × (64.07 g SO₂ / 1 mol) = 365 g.

questions.q: 4 NO + 6 H₂O → 4 NH₃ + 5 O₂ has an enthalpy change of 46.72 kJ. How many grams of ammonia can be produced if 32.5 kJ of heat energy are provided? Three sig figs.
2 H₂ (g) + O₂ (g) → 2 H₂O (l) has ΔH_rxn = −571 kJ. What is the enthalpy change if 1.00 gram of hydrogen reacts in this manner?
2 AB + 5/2 O₂ → 2 AO₂ + B₂O has ΔH = −465.8 kJ. How many kJ of heat are produced when 6.27 grams of AB combust? Three sig figs.
questions.note: 6.27 g ÷ 65.0 g/mol = 0.09646 mol AB × (465.8 kJ / 2 mol AB) = 22.5 kJ produced.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correctly written formation reaction for CaO (s)?
questions.note: A formation reaction makes exactly 1 mole of product from elements in their standard states (O₂ gas, not O atoms or ions), using fractions if needed.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correctly written formation reaction for NH₃ (g)?
questions.note: Exactly 1 mol NH₃ from N₂ (g) and H₂ (g), so the coefficients become fractions.

questions.q: Select the ΔH_f values that would be zero.
questions.note: ΔH_f = 0 only for an element in its STANDARD STATE at 25 °C: O₂ gas, H₂ gas, Zn solid. Bromine is a liquid, neon a gas, calcium a solid and nitrogen a gas, so the other phases aren't zero.

questions.q: Which two answers show correct set-ups for C₂H₄ (g) + 3 O₂ (g) → 2 H₂O (l) + 2 CO₂ (g)?
opts: Hrxn = Hf H₂O + Hf CO₂ − (Hf C₂H₄ + Hf O₂)
Hrxn = Hf C₂H₄ + 3·Hf O₂ − (2·Hf H₂O + 2·Hf CO₂)
questions.note: ΔH_rxn = Σ n·ΔH_f(products) − Σ n·ΔH_f(reactants), with coefficients. The second one is the same set-up with ΔH_f of O₂ already written as 0.

questions.q: Using enthalpies of formation, which is closest to the enthalpy change for CH₄ (g) + Cl₂ (g) → CH₃Cl (g) + HCl (g)?
questions.note: Products − reactants = (−81.9 + −92.307) − (−74.6 + 0) = −99.6 kJ → closest is −99.452 kJ. Cl₂ is an element, so its ΔH_f = 0.

questions.q: Using enthalpies of formation, which is closest to the enthalpy change for 3 CH₄ (g) + 2 H₂O (l) + CO₂ (g) → 4 CO (g) + 8 H₂ (g)?
Using the ΔH_f° values given, determine the enthalpy of AX₂ (g) + 2 Y₂ (g) → AX₂Y₄ (g). Round to the tenths place and include the unit.

questions.note: Reversing a reaction flips the sign of ΔH.

questions.q: Given A → B (ΔH = 70 kJ) and B → C (ΔH = −110 kJ), find each. Enter like "35 kJ".
questions.note: Multiply ΔH by the same factor as the equation; reversing flips the sign. 3 × 70 = 210; ½ × (−110) = −55; reverse and ×10: 10 × (−70) = −700.

questions.q: Given A → B (ΔH = −50 kJ) and B → C (ΔH = 20 kJ), combine them. Enter like "35 kJ".
questions.note: A → C: add both, −50 + 20 = −30 kJ. A + C → 2 B: A → B (−50) plus C → B (reverse of B → C, −20) = −70 kJ.

questions.q: What is the enthalpy change for 2 Cr (s) + 3 O₂ (g) → 2 CrO₃ (s)?
questions.note: Add the two equations: 4 Cr + 6 O₂ → 4 CrO₃, ΔH = −2256.8 + (−108.2) = −2365.0 kJ. Divide by 2 for the target: −1182.5 kJ.
questions.given: 4 Cr (s) + 3 O₂ (g) → 2 Cr₂O₃ (s), ΔH = −2256.8 kJ · 2 Cr₂O₃ (s) + 3 O₂ (g) → 4 CrO₃ (s), ΔH = −108.2 kJ

questions.q: Determine the enthalpy change for 2 E + X₂ → 2 EX. Round to the ones position and include the unit.
questions.note: 2 × (E + X₂ → EX₂) = −1088 kJ, then add 2 EX₂ → 2 EX + X₂ (521 kJ): −1088 + 521 = −567 kJ.
questions.given: E + X₂ → EX₂, ΔH = −544 kJ · 2 EX₂ → 2 EX + X₂, ΔH = 521 kJ

questions.q: What is the enthalpy change for 4 NH₃ (g) + 5 O₂ (g) → 4 NO (g) + 6 H₂O (l)?
questions.given: N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 NH₃, ΔH = −922.22 kJ · N₂ + O₂ → 2 NO, ΔH = 180.5 kJ · 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (l), ΔH = −571.6 kJ

questions.q: Determine the enthalpy change for X + Y + 3/2 Z₂ → XYZ₃. Round to the ones position and include the unit.
questions.note: Reverse eq. 1: X + ½ Z₂ → XZ, −549. Keep eq. 2: −649. Reverse eq. 3 and halve: XZ + YZ₂ → XYZ₃, −319.5. Sum = −1517.5 → −1518 kJ.
questions.given: XZ → X + ½ Z₂, ΔH = 549 kJ · Y + Z₂ → YZ₂, ΔH = −649 kJ · 2 XYZ₃ → 2 XZ + 2 YZ₂, ΔH = 639 kJ
